newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain one pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain one pct to new record.

text.p: The composite index at Istanbul's stock market rose 1.02 percent in selective activity on Wednesday to hit the sixth record close in a row in a medium-term uptrend continuing since mid-September.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 79,511.82, up 800 points from Tuesday's 78,711.82, the previous high. It surged 22.7 percent since September 13.
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.85 level, compared to around $1 in April.
"The market has lost the vitality it had last week, but selective activity continues in stocks that have posted less gains than the market index during the uptrend," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.

Trade volume shrank to 16 trillion lira from yesterday's 19.32 trillion, mainly due to the narrow morning trade when the index was squeezed in a tight range around 79,000 resistance after failing to break this barrier earlier in the week.
"I expect the index to drift within 79,000-81,000 range for a while after the rapid rise from the 70,000 level," said Yalcin Arican from Hak securities.
"Positive factors fuelling the uptrend are the Treasury's ability to borrow at hefty amounts, downward t-bill yields and the lack of significant activity in the dollar," he added.

The Treasury sold a record 288.2 trillion lira worth 238-day t-bills in an auction on Tuesday at sligtly lower yields. Bids also reached a record 480.6 trillion for the t-bills which carried the longest maturity issued so far this year.
Brokers said a major correction awaited to the ongoing uptrend remained overdue.
"The market should take a breath, but I am not sure that this will happen. A boom in trade volume is needed for a major selling to take place," said Murad Kuran who owns a brokerage.
Of the 225 shares traded, 89 declined, 76 advanced and 60 were stable. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.41 percent to 85,022.32 and the 15-share financial index leapt 2.45 percent to 74,901.68.

Top actives were utilities Cukurova Elektrik, down 1,000 lira at 76,000 and its associate Kepez Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 82,000, followed by motor vehicle producer Otosan, up 3,500 lira at 35,500 and T.Isbank's C series shares, steady at 13,000 lira. -- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
